summary.text: A 44 year old woman was admitted in April 2018 with localized small cell lung cancer (T2N1M0) with mediastinal lymph node metastases, no driver gene alterations and PD-L1 expression in under 1% of tumor cells. She received first-line etoposide and cisplatin, then developed aggravated dry cough and dyspnea with tumor regrowth and superior vena cava obstruction syndrome.

In June 2018 she received thoracic radiotherapy and second-line irinotecan and carboplatin with significant symptom improvement. In September 2018 cough and shortness of breath returned; CT showed new bilateral ground-glass opacities, cultures were negative, and radiation-induced pneumonitis was diagnosed and improved gradually on steroid. In January 2019 bone and supraclavicular nodal metastases appeared, and nab-paclitaxel failed.

She received atezolizumab for six cycles with local radiotherapy, then in June 2019 developed liver and brain metastases and started nivolumab. One week later she had cough and fever; CT and negative cultures led to a suspected grade 2 immunotherapy-related pneumonitis, treated with intravenous methylprednisolone with improvement on day 15. On day 24 grade 3 pneumonitis reoccurred with oxygen saturation of 88%.

High-dose methylprednisolone restarted after multidisciplinary discussion but did not help within 5 days, and Klebsiella pneumoniae bacterial pneumonia was diagnosed without response to antibiotics. With continued steroid plus infliximab, mycophenolate mofetil and IVIG, symptoms, oxygen saturation and radiographic findings improved significantly; a later CT showed progressive disease in the liver.

Figure 3
Immune-related pneumonitis. (A) A CT scan showed no any inflammatory lesions in the lungs following the treatment with first PD-L1 inhibitor atezolizumab. (E) High-dose intravenous corticosteroid therapy did not alleviate her symptoms within 5 days, with worsening radiographic findings. (F) After she received immunosuppressive agents including infliximab, mycophenolate mofetil and human immunoglobulin, fever, dry cough, and dyspnea were relieved significantly, with a significant improvement of pulmonary inflammation. White arrow indicates inflammatory lesions.
